front.title: ActivityPub++: One Federated Carrier for Activities, Events, Agent Messages and Payments

abstract.t: This document specifies ActivityPub++, a profile that composes ActivityPub, CloudEvents, the Agent2Agent protocol and x402 into a single federated carrier. An ActivityPub activity carries one CloudEvents envelope; the envelope's data is one A2A message; the message carries one content-addressed object, and carries payment or authority only when it actually states them. Nodes that implement the profile form a federated network the authors call the Semioverse.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: ActivityPub++ is the profile a node speaks to join the Semioverse, the 561 Group's federated network named after the Fediverse. It composes four open protocols into one nesting instead of four neighbouring services: an ActivityPub activity carries one CloudEvents envelope, whose data is one A2A message, whose single part is a content-addressed SEN object. Payment and authority (x402, UCAN, CapTP, an EVM anchor) appear only inside that A2A message, when the message actually carries them. This document states that nesting as requirements, so that a second implementation can interoperate with the house one without reading its code. It is derived from the Semioverse term, the activitypub-services-section README, "Union transport", and the projection and extraction the house code enforces in sen-activity.mjs.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

li.t: Node: a server that speaks ActivityPub++. The Semioverse is the network of nodes, not a server; its intended server is MOOSE, which no package yet carries.
Actor: an ActivityPub actor hosted by a node.
SEN object: a value in the house semiotic expression notation, encoded as the canonical normalized-content envelope and carried as application/sen+cbor bytes.
Envelope: the CloudEvents event that carries one A2A message.
ni name: an RFC 6920 ni:///sha-256; URI naming bytes by their SHA-256 digest (Naming Things with Hashes ).

section.name: One Public Face
section.t: A node federates through ActivityPub and nothing beside it. ActivityPub supplies actors, inboxes, outboxes and delivery; Activity Streams 2.0 supplies the vocabulary; WebFinger and NodeInfo make actors and nodes discoverable.
A node MUST give each actor exactly one public ActivityPub face, at the actor URL `<origin>/actors/<identifier>`.
A node MUST NOT expose a public A2A listener beside its ActivityPub face; A2A is the operation language inside the federated carrier, not a second public transport.
A node MUST verify the signature or proof on every inbound activity before its inbox callback runs, and offer no unsigned-admission mode.
A node that has no receiving workflow for an actor MUST answer a POST to that actor's inbox with 405 rather than accept and discard the activity.

section.name: The Activity
section.t: An ActivityPub++ activity is an ordinary ActivityStreams activity whose object is one document naming one envelope.
An ActivityPub++ activity MUST have type `Accept`, `Announce`, `Create`, `Offer`, `Reject` or `Update`.
The activity's object MUST be one `Document` with `mediaType` `application/sen+cbor`, whose `name` is the ni name of the envelope bytes and whose `url` is one `Link` with the same media type.
The object's link MUST carry the envelope bytes as one canonical base64 `data:application/sen+cbor` URI.
A receiver MUST reject an activity whose inline envelope bytes do not hash to the object's `name`.
A sender MUST keep the inline envelope bytes nonempty and at most 262,144 bytes.
A receiver MUST reject inline envelope bytes that are larger than 262,144 bytes or not canonically encoded.
The activity MUST name exactly one A2A Agent Card, as an `attachment` `Link` with `mediaType` `application/json` and `name` "A2A Agent Card".
The actor origin, the recipient and the Agent Card URL MUST use HTTPS, except on loopback addresses during development.
A sender SHOULD derive the activity's `id` from its type, actor, recipient, envelope ni name and Agent Card, so that republishing the same activity yields the same identity.

section.name: The Envelope
section.t: The envelope is a CloudEvents event (CloudEvents specification ) whose fields bind it to the activity that carries it.
The envelope MUST have `specversion` "1.0" and exactly the attributes `id`, `specversion`, `source`, `type`, `time`, `subject`, `datacontenttype` and `data`.
A receiver MUST reject an envelope whose `source` is not the activity's actor or whose `subject` is not the recipient it was addressed to.
The envelope's `type` MUST be `org.harmonious-union.activitypub.<activity type in lower case>.v1`, matching the carrying activity's type.

The envelope MUST declare `datacontenttype` `application/a2a+json` and carry `data` with exactly `profile` "org.harmonious-union.activitypub.cloudevent.a2a-sen.v1", `transport` "A2A" and one A2A `message`.
The envelope's `id` MUST be the ni name of the envelope's canonical body without its `id`.
A receiver MUST reject an envelope whose `id` does not name its canonical body.
The envelope's `time` MUST be an RFC 3339 timestamp.

section.name: The Agent Message
section.t: The envelope's data is one message in the Agent2Agent protocol (Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol ). The message, not the activity, is where the operation is stated.
The message MUST have role `ROLE_USER` or `ROLE_AGENT`.
The message MUST carry exactly one raw part with `mediaType` `application/sen+cbor`.
That part MUST state the ni name of its bytes in `metadata.ni`.
A receiver MUST reject a SEN part whose bytes do not match its `metadata.ni`.
The part's bytes MUST be canonical normalized SEN content, so that equal values have equal bytes and equal names.
A node SHOULD publish a signed Agent Card, so that a receiver can check the card was issued by the domain it names.

section.name: Authority and Payment
section.t: Payment and authority ride inside the agent message. They are never sibling labels on the activity. Payment is x402 .
A node MUST NOT mark an activity as carrying UCAN, CapTP, x402 or an EVM anchor unless its A2A message actually carries that authority, invocation, settlement or anchor.
A node that prices an operation MUST state the price and settle it as x402 version 2 payment requirements and payloads.

A node carrying an x402 exchange inside an A2A message SHOULD use the message metadata keys of the A2A x402 extension (`x402.payment.status`, `x402.payment.required`, `x402.payment.payload`, `x402.payment.receipts`).
A node MUST NOT treat a settled payment as authority to perform an operation that its own admission has not accepted; payment proves a payment event and nothing more.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: This section records the status of known implementations of the protocol defined by this specification at the time of posting of this Internet-Draft, and is based on a proposal described in . It is to be removed before publication as an RFC.

section.name: House activitypub-services-section
section.t: src/sen-activity.mjs projects (projectSenActivity) and extracts (extractSenActivity) the whole nesting and enforces every MUST in The Activity, The Envelope and The Agent Message. The provider (src/provider.mjs) is built on Fedify and supplies WebFinger, NodeInfo 2.1, signature verification and delivery.

section.name: House a2a-services-section and x402-services-section
section.t: scripts/sen-part.mjs builds and checks the SEN part; scripts/agent-card-signing.mjs signs Agent Cards. The x402 section is the one x402 v2 payment boundary. No house code yet carries an x402 exchange inside an A2A message.

section.name: Nodes
section.t: On 2026-09-27 no node runs this profile as one server: ActivityPub, A2A and x402 each still have their own HTTP carrier in separate sections, which the one-public-face requirement forbids for a conforming node. MOOSE, the intended node server, has no package.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Every carried byte is named by its digest, so a receiver detects substitution of the envelope or the SEN object; the digests do not authenticate the sender, which is the job of the signature every inbound activity carries.

The envelope binds its source and subject to the activity's actor and recipient, so an envelope lifted from one activity and replayed inside another addressed elsewhere is rejected. An identical activity replayed to the same recipient has the same id, which lets a receiver's idempotency custody detect it.
The inline size bound limits the cost of verifying an activity before its signature is checked.
Payment carried inside an agent message inherits the risks of x402 itself: payments applied to the wrong resource, duplicate settlement, overdrawn allowances and delivery on payments that fail.
A node that sells an operation MUST bind each payment to the exact operation it pays for, and settle it before performing the operation or bear the loss.
Activities addressed to the public collection are readable by anyone, and a payer's address is public on its settlement network; neither is suitable for material its parties need to keep private.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This revision makes no request of IANA. It uses two media types that are not registered, application/sen+cbor and application/a2a+json; registering them, or replacing them with registered types, is an open issue.

section.name: Open Issues
section.t: Each issue below would become a requirement once the dependency named with it is resolved. This appendix is to be removed before publication as an RFC.

li.t: Which x402 version the A2A carriage uses. Resolution is blocked by: the A2A x402 extension v0.1 references x402 version 1, while this profile requires version 2.

Whether node-to-node settlement replication travels inside ActivityPub like other activities. Resolution is blocked by: MetroPlat federation now posts CloudEvents to a peer's /arrivals route and signs transfers with RFC 9421, a second channel beside the one public face.

Whether the envelope type and profile keep the org.harmonious-union prefix. Resolution is blocked by: a naming decision; renaming changes every envelope type string and breaks interoperation with existing activities.
Whether application/sen+cbor and application/a2a+json are registered. Resolution is blocked by: a stable SEN encoding specification to cite in a registration request.
Which inbound signature schemes a conforming node must accept. Resolution is blocked by: a survey of what deployed Fediverse peers send (HTTP Signatures drafts, RFC 9421, Data Integrity proofs).
